title: Grandfathered Privileged Access Under the Tightened PAM Policy
scenario_text:
Quenby Systems tightened its Privileged Access Management (PAM) policy in late 2024.

Version 2 (effective January 1, 2023) states: "Privileged (production admin) access may be granted for a term of up to 12 months and must be recertified annually."

Version 3 (effective October 1, 2024) states: "Privileged access may be granted for a maximum term of 90 days, requires a registered hardware security key for authentication, and must be recertified quarterly." v3 includes a transition clause: "Grants that are active as of September 30, 2024 remain valid under their original 12-month expiry (v2 terms) until their next scheduled recertification date. At that recertification, the grant must be re-provisioned under v3 (90-day term, hardware key). Any grant issued on or after October 1, 2024 is governed by v3 from issuance."

The CyberArk record for grant G-3345 (engineer: L. Duarte, scope: prod-admin) shows: Grant Date 2024-05-15, Expiry Date 2025-05-15, Next Recertification Date 2025-05-15 (annual). The grant has been continuously active. It is currently 2025-02-10.

A security engineer posts in #access-review on 2025-02-10: "Auditing prod-admin grants. G-3345 predates the 90-day rule. Do we have to convert it to a 90-day hardware-key grant right now, or does it ride until its recert?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the PAM record, determine G-3345's current status and when it must move to v3.
question: What is the correct handling of grant G-3345 as of 2025-02-10?
choices: G-3345 remains valid under v2 until its 2025-05-15 recertification, at which point it must be re-provisioned under v3 (90-day term, hardware key).
G-3345 must be converted to a 90-day hardware-key grant immediately, because v3 took effect October 1, 2024 and supersedes all prior grants.
G-3345 expired on October 1, 2024 when v3's 90-day maximum took effect, and access must be re-requested from scratch.
G-3345 remains under v2 terms indefinitely, because it was issued before October 1, 2024 and is continuously active.
